item.title: Texas PUC adopts softened rules on data center interconnection
item.description: Utility Dive — The Public Utility Commission of Texas backed off the standards it proposed in March, eliminating a non-refundable interconnection fee, halving its financial security requirement and extending energization milestone deadlines.

item.title: Federal judge restores $7B Solar for All program, says EPA illegally axed it
item.description: Utility Dive — A Trump-appointed judge said the One Big Beautiful Bill Act did not convert the funding into “a lump-sum amount subject to EPA’s discretion.” Defendants acted contrary to Congress’ intent and with “no other statutory authority” when they terminated it, she said.

item.title: NorthStar Clean Energy powers on 120-MW Michigan solar project
item.description: Solar Power World — NorthStar Clean Energy has completed its 120-MW Hart Solar Project in Oceana County, Michigan, which is generating enough clean electricity power more than 21,000 homes. Executive Energy Services and the Michigan Public Power Agency (MPPA) have signed power purchase agreements on portions of Hart Solar’s output. “Hart Solar is an important investment in Michigan’s energy…

item.title: Corsica Sole switches on 150 kW electrolyzer at 12 MW solar plant
item.description: PV Magazine — Corsica Sole has commissioned a 150 kW green hydrogen facility at its 12 MW Folelli solar plant in Corsica to convert otherwise-curtailed solar power into hydrogen. The facility can produce around 20 kg of hydrogen per day and store up to 230 kg for use in maritime transport and other local applications.

item.title: Newsom vetoes bill to create California PUC inspector general
item.description: Utility Dive — Newsom signed several other bills with direct or indirect implications for electric utilities and power infrastructure stakeholders, including Assembly Bill 192 standing up the transmission infrastructure accelerator.

item.title: U.S. solar module production reaches historic 100 GW landmark
item.description: PV Magazine — The United States crossed 100 GW of cumulative solar PV module production during Q2 2026, according to a new bottom-up factory-level analysis by Terawatt PV Research going back to the early 1970’s. Almost two-fifths of all module production can be attributed to First Solar - a reflection of the company's unique role in U.S. manufacturing dating back more than 20 years.

item.title: Malaysia sets fixed grid charge, 10-year contracts for corporate solar
item.description: PV Magazine — The Malaysian government has unveiled a package of measures to accelerate its Corporate Renewable Energy Supply Scheme, including a fixed grid-access charge for firm power and mandatory 10-year contracts, aimed at improving project bankability and encouraging development.

item.title: New York regulators approve 90-mile transmission line
item.description: Utility Dive — The $3.3-billion project aims to improve downstate power delivery by 2030. It is being developed by New York Transco and the New York Power Authority.

item.title: Chinese scientists build 33.3%-efficient perovskite-silicon tandem solar cell processed in ambient air
item.description: PV Magazine — Chinese researchers developed a PNCC polymer hole-transport layer that enables efficient and stable perovskite solar cells to be fabricated under ambient conditions. The material was used in a perovskite-silicon tandem cell that achieved 33.3% efficiency and a certified efficiency of 33.0%.

item.title: Canada trade tribunal rescinds order on Chinese solar modules, laminates
item.description: PV Magazine — Canada's trade tribunal has terminated a five-year review of anti-dumping and countervailing duties on Chinese solar modules and laminates, rescinding the order after finding the review lacked domestic-producer support.

item.title: Trump-appointed judge restores $7 billion Solar for All program
item.description: Solar Power World — A federal judge has ruled that the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) unlawfully canceled the $7 billion Solar for All program, striking down the agency’s decision to end a nationwide program designed to lower electricity bills and bring affordable solar power to families and communities across the country. “The court ruled the Trump administration never should…

item.title: Google-backed pilot demonstrates hourly carbon accounting for US BESS using granular certificates
item.description: Energy Storage News — A US battery storage pilot sponsored by tech giant Google has demonstrated how batteries can capture surplus renewable energy and deliver it during hours with greater fossil generation.

item.title: US energy storage industry targets 225GW/1TWh deployment by end of 2032, according to Energy Storage Coalition
item.description: Energy Storage News — The US energy storage industry is targeting 225GW/1TWh of storage deployment by the end of 2032, according to an analysis published by the Energy Storage Coalition (ESC).

item.title: Logistics and transportation trends coming to solar projects soon
item.description: Solar Power World — As the products used in solar and storage projects evolve, their new forms affect more than just installation layouts. Third-party logistics companies (3PLs) must adapt to changes in product design as well. A pallet of residential solar panels from 10 years ago was shipped much differently than the 7-ft long panels of today. The same…

item.title: Finland proposes priority system for grid connections
item.description: PV Magazine — Finland’s government is proposing a priority system for electricity network connections in areas of scarce grid capacity in a bid to incentivise large electricity consumers and standalone storage systems to locate in areas where the grid is less congested.

item.title: Poland market shifting to ‘selective, capital-disciplined phase where execution quality matters’
item.description: Energy Storage News — Poland's grid-scale storage market has reached an impressive scale in the last few years, helped by the capacity market and various government schemes, but numerous challenges now need to be overcome.

item.title: Fluence and Eve Energy agree 206GWh battery supply deal
item.description: Energy Storage News — System integrator Fluence and lithium-ion battery OEM Eve Energy have struck a massive 206GWh battery supply framework agreement for 2027-31, one of the largest deals of its kind ever announced.

item.title: Already-operating battery storage projects are key to making the business case for the next assets bankable
item.description: Energy Storage News — Existing assets can provide crucial benchmarks in sizing and other crucial battery storage design decisions, writes Ashutosh Vats, head of BESS business development at 3E.

item.title: India flow battery player Delectrik talks 100MWh NTPC project award, targets gigawatt-hour order book
item.description: Energy Storage News — Vishal Mittal, founder and CEO of Delectrik makes the case for flow batteries to meet India’s long-duration needs in an exclusive ESN Premium interview.

item.title: French startup repurposes EV batteries for solar energy storage
item.description: PV Magazine — Battwoo is repurposing electric vehicle batteries for stationary energy storage, targeting solar self-consumption and other commercial and industrial applications. The company says its refurbished systems can cost around 30% less than new batteries while extending battery service life by several decades.

item.title: Predictive control cuts costs in buildings combining PV, heat pumps, EVs, thermal storage
item.description: PV Magazine — Researchers have developed a predictive rule-based control strategy for building energy systems integrating PV, heat pumps, thermal storage, and electric vehicles. Simulations show it can approach model predictive control performance while substantially reducing computational requirements and operating costs compared with conventional rule-based control.

item.title: Study finds potential for 150 GW of additional PV at substations in Germany
item.description: PV Magazine — A Fraunhofer IEE study estimates that battery storage could enable around 150 GW of additional PV capacity to connect at 1,313 rural substations in Germany. By absorbing generation peaks, storage could improve utilization of existing transformers while limiting average PV curtailment to around 1%.

item.title: Ohio Commission Advances AES Acquisition
item.description: RTO Insider — PUCO has approved a change in ownership for AES Ohio, but with an unusual proviso barring members of the company’s board from participating in all decision-making related to data centers if they have “pecuniary interests” in the industry.

item.title: BPA Seeks $250M Rate Increase Following Spill Order
item.description: RTO Insider — The Bonneville Power Administration said it could hike power prices to mitigate a potential $250 million revenue shortfall after a federal judge ordered the agency to increase spill over dams to protect migrating salmon.

item.title: Utah-Nevada Tx Line Aims to Spur Geothermal Development
item.description: RTO Insider — The Bureau of Land Management has opened public comment for Silver Rock Transmission, a proposed 330-mile, up-to-600-kV line BLM says will help facilitate geothermal leasing in Nevada and Utah.

item.title: Congestion Forces SPP to Issue Brief EEA Level 1
item.description: RTO Insider — SPP says congestion issues on the eastern seam of its eastern balancing authority area led to the region’s first energy emergency alert in two years.

item.title: MISO Stakeholders Repeat Calls for Fair Cost Splits on Large Load Tx Work
item.description: RTO Insider — MISO stakeholders are increasingly concerned about the potential for cost spillover from large load customers who require increasingly complex transmission projects onto the RTO’s other customers and said so in front of the RTO’s board of directors.

item.title: Is Compensating Utility Customers for Power Outages a Good Idea?
item.description: RTO Insider — Electric utilities rarely compensate their customers for power outages, regardless of their duration and the damage they caused.

item.title: N.Y. PSC Directs Utilities to Report How They Use AI
item.description: RTO Insider — The order is a first step to assess utility AI use and could lead to regulations designed to minimize risks.

item.title: From 10-97% SOC in 9 minutes: Sunwoda joins the flash charging race
item.description: Electrek — Chinese battery brand Sunwoda has just revealed a new EV battery charging system that can add 100 km (~62 miles) of range to an EV every minute, and can take a battery from from 10-97% SOC in less than 10 minutes. At room temperature . more…
